candidates.source_name: SiStat podatkovna baza (SURS statistical database, PxWeb)
candidates.why_relevant: Master machine-readable repository of every SURS statistical table, including retail turnover, household final consumption (COICOP), ICT/internet use and enterprise online sales. This is the denominator layer for normalising card/POS/ATM payment volumes.
candidates.legal_status: official statistics; reuse permitted with attribution to SURS
candidates.suggested_collection_method: PxWeb REST API (JSON-stat/CSV/PX) with periodic table-level polling; drive from the changelog API to detect updates
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from SURS news items to underlying tables
queries_used: SiStat podatkovna baza SURS API PxWeb open data

candidates.source_name: SiStat PxWeb API help / documentation (Pomoč pri uporabi API-ja)
candidates.why_relevant: Documents the exact endpoints, request shapes, rate limits and output formats (PX, CSV, JSON, XLSX, JSON-stat) needed to build a durable automated collector against SiStat, plus the changelog API for update detection.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off fetch of the help page and the Slovenian API PDF; re-check annually

candidates.source_name: SURS StatWeb — Uporaba IKT v gospodinjstvih (ICT usage in households, incl. online shopping and payment methods)
candidates.why_relevant: The annual EU-harmonised ICT household survey is the only official national source for the share of individuals shopping online and, critically, HOW they paid (debit/credit card vs cash on delivery vs bank transfer). Directly measures card-vs-cash behaviour in e-commerce.
candidates.source_subtype: survey programme landing page + First Release series
candidates.legal_status: official statistics, free reuse with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual scrape of the Field page for new First Releases; pair with the underlying SiStat ICT tables via API
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query (sl) then snowball from news item to programme page
queries_used: SURS uporaba interneta nakupovanje po spletu plačila statistika
local_language_terms_used: plačilo z debetno ali kreditno kartico

candidates.source_name: SURS StatWeb — Uporaba IKT v podjetjih / Spletna prodaja (enterprise ICT & online sales)
candidates.why_relevant: Supply side of e-commerce: share of enterprises selling online and online-sales revenue as % of turnover — the merchant-acceptance denominator for e-commerce acquiring and card-not-present volumes.
candidates.source_subtype: survey programme (ICT-PODJ, running since 2004) + First Releases
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual fetch of First Release + SiStat enterprise ICT tables
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on e-poslovanje/spletna prodaja
queries_used: SURS IKT uporaba v podjetjih e-poslovanje spletna prodaja statistika

candidates.source_name: SURS — Trgovina na drobno: prihodek od prodaje (retail trade turnover, monthly)
candidates.why_relevant: Monthly and annual retail turnover in value and volume terms is the core denominator for POS transaction value, card penetration of retail spend, and seasonality modelling of terminal throughput.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly PxWeb API pull of retail turnover tables; cross-check against the monthly First Release text
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query (sl)

candidates.source_name: SURS — Anketa o porabi v gospodinjstvih (APG / Household Budget Survey)
candidates.why_relevant: Detailed household expenditure structure by category, plus savings and indebtedness and durable-goods equipment. Underpins CPI weights and gives the spending basket against which payment-instrument use is normalised.
candidates.access_status: open (aggregates); microdata via SURS researcher access
candidates.legal_status: official statistics; microdata subject to statistical confidentiality
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch survey methodology doc and First Releases; pull APG tables from SiStat on each wave (multi-annual cadence)
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on household expenditure survey
queries_used: SURS anketa o porabi v gospodinjstvih izdatki gospodinjstev APG

candidates.source_name: SURS — Izdatki gospodinjstev za končno potrošnjo po COICOP 2018 (national accounts table 0301941S)
candidates.why_relevant: National-accounts household final consumption expenditure by COICOP purpose, 1995 onwards, current and constant prices. The single most reliable long time series for sizing addressable payment value by spend category.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PxWeb API pull of tables 0301941S (COICOP 2018) and legacy 0301940S (COICOP 1999) for backward continuity
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from national accounts search to concrete PxWeb table ids

candidates.why_relevant: Household disposable income distribution, material deprivation and (in ad-hoc modules) over-indebtedness and financial exclusion — the basis for segmenting who can realistically hold cards/accounts and who remains cash-dependent.

candidates.why_relevant: Full English mirror of SURS releases and metadata — removes translation risk for the analytical layer while remaining the same authoritative dataset. Also hosts the publications catalogue and annual national-statistics reports.

candidates.source_name: SURS microdata access for researchers (varna soba / oddaljeni dostop)
candidates.why_relevant: Route to individual-level ICT, APG and SILC microdata — the only way to cross-tabulate payment-method use by income, age and region rather than relying on published marginals. Governed by an approval committee (ORA).
candidates.access_status: restricted — application, committee approval, secure room or remote access
candidates.legal_status: statistical confidentiality; research purposes only, no redistribution of microdata

candidates.source_name: OPSI — Odprti podatki Slovenije (national open data portal)
candidates.why_relevant: CKAN-based national catalogue that re-publishes SURS tables (as surs<tableid> datasets) and AJPES registers with stable dataset URIs and machine-readable resources. Excellent discovery layer and a stable alternative access path when stat.si structure changes.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: CKAN package_search API filtered on publisher SURS / AJPES; snapshot dataset metadata for change detection
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for national open data portal; snowballed from SURS table ids appearing there

candidates.source_name: AJPES — Javna objava letnih poročil (JOLP, public annual reports)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory filing point for all Slovenian companies including banks and payment institutions. Gives audited balance sheets and P&L for acquirers, PSPs, retail chains and ATM operators — the firm-level ground truth behind aggregate payment statistics.
candidates.access_status: free but requires registration; hard daily cap of 20 business subjects per user account
candidates.legal_status: public disclosure mandated by the Companies Act (ZGD-1); rate limit is an explicit anti-scraping control that must be respected
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/low-volume targeted retrieval of a watchlist of entities within the 20/day cap; never bulk-crawl. Combine with the JOLP publication calendar to time pulls (2025 reports published 5 Aug 2026).
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on statutory annual report disclosure
queries_used: AJPES letna poročila JOLP javna objava podatkov Slovenija podjetja
candidates.observed_blocker: Documented free registration requirement and a 20-business-subjects-per-day-per-account limit stated to protect the information system

candidates.why_relevant: Central register of all Slovenian business entities, partially opened as a twice-monthly XML dump. Enables building a NACE-filtered universe of retailers, payment institutions and e-commerce merchants — the entity backbone for merchant/terminal density analysis.
candidates.legal_status: open data; published by AJPES as public register extract
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Twice-monthly download and diff of the XML dump; index by matična številka and SKD/NACE activity code
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from OPSI catalogue search

candidates.why_relevant: Enumerates every register and public service AJPES operates (PRS, JOLP, eVPO, RNO, statistical surveys), which is the fastest way to discover further structured datasets relevant to merchant and financial-entity mapping.

candidates.why_relevant: Government macroeconomic analysis office that interprets SURS retail and consumption data monthly, often with commentary and breakdowns published before the underlying tables are easy to assemble. candidates.source_name: FURS — Davčno potrjevanje računov (fiscalisation of receipts)
candidates.why_relevant: Every cash-business receipt in Slovenia is confirmed in real time by the tax administration, and the legal definition of 'gotovinsko poslovanje' explicitly covers banknotes, coins, payment and credit cards and cheques. If any aggregate of this dataset is published, it is the highest-resolution national proxy for POS transaction counts and cash-vs-card mix.
candidates.access_status: system itself is not public; only guidance documents and any published aggregates were found
candidates.legal_status: tax secrecy over transaction-level data; aggregates would be public-sector information, potentially obtainable via an information-of-public-character request
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor FURS statistical publications and annual reports for fiscalisation aggregates; consider a formal ZDIJZ information request for aggregated receipt counts by payment type
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles reasoning (who must record payment-instrument use by law) then local-language search
queries_used: FURS davčne blagajne statistika izdani računi način plačila podatki

negative_findings.description: NIJZ (Nacionalni inštitut za javno zdravje) was named in the cell definition but is a public-health institute; no payment, retail-turnover or e-commerce statistics were identified in its remit during this scouting pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: No NIJZ dataset relevant to payment demand denominators was found. NIJZ appears to be included in the cell only as a stylistic example of 'AJPES-style official national statistics', not as a genuine source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Spending further collection effort on NIJZ would be wasted; AJPES and FURS are the correct non-SURS official-register members of this cell.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Slovenian for published FURS statistics broken down by payment method (cash vs card) derived from the davčne blagajne fiscalisation system.
negative_findings.result_summary: Found the legal framework and taxpayer guidance confirming that card and cash receipts are both fiscalised, but found no public statistical release aggregating receipts by payment instrument.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This would be the highest-resolution national cash-vs-card measure in existence for Slovenia. Its apparent non-publication means the cash/card split must be inferred from ICT survey self-reports and central-bank statistics instead, or requested formally.

negative_findings.description: AJPES JOLP, the statutory annual-report repository, was assessed for automated collection feasibility.
negative_findings.result_summary: Documentation states free registration is required and a hard limit of 20 business subjects per user account per day applies, explicitly to protect the information system.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collection design that assumes bulk retrieval of Slovenian company financials from AJPES will fail and may be treated as abuse. A curated watchlist approach is required.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Slovenian for SURS-published measures of bank-account ownership or financial exclusion at household level.
negative_findings.result_summary: EU-SILC covers income, poverty, deprivation and indebtedness, and an ad-hoc 2008 module addressed debt and financial exclusion, but no recurring official SURS indicator of account/card ownership was identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Financial-inclusion denominators for Slovenia will have to come from the central bank or supranational sources (e.g. World Bank Findex, ECB), not the national statistical office. This is a genuine boundary of this coverage cell.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell supplies denominators only. Actual payment, card, ATM and POS transaction counts for Slovenia are published by Banka Slovenije and the ECB, which fall outside this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Ensure the Banka Slovenije / ECB payment-statistics cell is scouted, and define the join keys (period, NACE where available) so SURS denominators and central-bank numerators can be aligned.

coverage_gaps.description: Eurostat re-publishes the Slovenian ICT household/enterprise survey, HBS and national accounts in harmonised form with a stable bulk-download API, which was not explored in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout Eurostat dataset codes (isoc_ec_*, isoc_e_*, nama_10_co3_p3, hbs_*) as an alternative, more automatable access path with cross-country comparability.

coverage_gaps.description: No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed live by this agent; all URLs come from search-result evidence and cross-references between sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass over all example_urls, treating any 403 as bot-defence rather than death and re-checking stat.si DocSysFile PDF ids, which are opaque and prone to rotation.

coverage_gaps.description: SURS retail turnover and ICT indicators are national and, at best, cohesion-region level; no municipality-level or merchant-category-level breakdown suitable for terminal-density modelling was identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Combine the AJPES PRS business register (entity-level, with addresses and SKD codes) with SURS structural business statistics to synthesise sub-national merchant density rather than expecting SURS to publish it.

coverage_gaps.description: The household budget survey (APG) runs only every few years while payment statistics are monthly or quarterly, and the COICOP 1999 to COICOP 2018 switch introduces a break in the consumption series.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Anchor high-frequency normalisation on monthly retail turnover and quarterly national accounts, and use APG only for structural basket weights; explicitly record the COICOP break date in the series metadata.

brief: Slovenia's denominator layer for payments intelligence is unusually well-consolidated: SURS publishes everything through one PxWeb database (SiStat) with a documented REST API in PX/CSV/JSON-stat, mirrored dataset-by-dataset on the national open data portal OPSI, and scheduled in advance via a public release calendar — so this cell can be collected deterministically rather than scraped. The highest-value series are monthly retail turnover, national-accounts household final consumption by COICOP, and the annual EU-harmonised ICT household survey, the last of which uniquely reports how online purchases were paid for (card versus cash on delivery versus bank transfer) and is therefore the only SURS-side direct read on card-versus-cash behaviour. Beyond SURS, AJPES supplies the statutory entity and financial-statement layer — its business register is open bulk XML, but JOLP annual reports are gated behind registration and a hard 20-subjects-per-day cap that forbids bulk collection — while FURS's real-time receipt fiscalisation captures cash-versus-card at transaction level but appears not to publish aggregates. The cell's hard boundary is that SURS produces no payment, card, ATM or POS transaction counts and no recurring account-ownership indicator; those must come from Banka Slovenije, the ECB, or Eurostat mirrors, which should be scouted separately and joined to these denominators.
